How these sites were made

Each project site on a.skh.am carries one of three labels in its footer, saying how much of the project was written by a person and how much by AI agents.

Made by hand

Written by hand, mostly before 2026; since then agents have only cleaned up or fixed bugs.

  • None yet

Made with agents

Built by a person and AI agents working together.

  • None yet

Made by agents

Built by AI agents from specs and configuration, with light human steering.

  • None yet

Not labelled yet: /advent, /agent-utils, /aish, /android-utils, /annum, /cacophony, /caravan, /collective, /cost, /crossbow, /ctx, /io-mcp, /kittui, /mcp-cli, /nix-reflect, /nlir, /omni-cli, /owt, /panopticon, /paratenic, /pi-daemon, /pulseaudio-lambda, /quaalude, /ring-mods, /slick, /stack, /tendril, /tools.

How projects were classified

From each repository's history: how many commits were made before 2026, how many were landed by the agent fleet (its commits are authored as Cacophony Daemon), co-author trailers naming an AI model, and when agent instruction files first appeared. The author then checked every label, and the author's call stands where the numbers are close.

The labels describe the code, not the sites themselves, which were all written by agents.
